---
title: "Example reports"
---

```{r, include = FALSE}
knitr::opts_chunk$set(echo = FALSE)
runs <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON("../../pkgdown/assets/example-reports.json"), error = function(e) NULL)
if (is.null(runs)) runs <- tryCatch(jsonlite::fromJSON("../example-reports.json"), error = function(e) NULL)
fmt <- function(x) format(x, big.mark = ",", scientific = FALSE, trim = TRUE)
```

Two reports from `render_report()`, both run against the full
[Fake NHS Trust synthetic dataset](https://github.com/ThomUK/synthetic-hospital-data)
read through its `fakehospdata` package, leaving out its `answers` schema (the
mess log and truth tables are the dataset's answer key, not part of the
trust's warehouse). Each report is a single self-contained HTML page with
three tabs, one per phase, and every table in it can be filtered and
downloaded. They are regenerated by the `example-reports` workflow on the
repository's Actions tab, run by hand.

```{r runs, results = "asis"}
if (is.null(runs) || nrow(runs) == 0) {
  cat("The reports have not been generated yet. Run the `example-reports` workflow from the Actions tab.\n")
} else {
  tab <- data.frame(
    Report = runs$label,
    Dataset = paste0(runs$scale, " set"),
    `Sampling threshold` = ifelse(is.infinite(runs$sample_rows), "none", paste(fmt(runs$sample_rows), "rows")),
    Tables = runs$tables, `Tables sampled` = runs$tables_sampled, Columns = runs$columns,
    `Rows in total` = fmt(runs$rows),
    `Phases 2 and 3` = ifelse(runs$tables_sampled > 0,
      "Phase 1 only: this was a sampled check, where not every row of the largest tables was reviewed. The full check below shows phases 2 and 3.",
      paste("Shown:", runs$fk_candidates, "foreign key candidates and the table clusters")),
    `Run time` = ifelse(runs$seconds >= 60, sprintf("%.0f min", runs$seconds / 60), paste(runs$seconds, "s")),
    Rendered = runs$rendered_at, check.names = FALSE
  )
  print(knitr::kable(tab))
}
```

```{r links, results = "asis"}
if (!is.null(runs) && nrow(runs) > 0) {
  blurb <- c(
    sampled = paste(
      "The default way to run the package on a large warehouse. Every table is inventoried and every column profiled,",
      "but tables above the sampling threshold are profiled on a sample of their rows, so the run is quick and the",
      "largest tables cost no more than the smallest. Phase 1 is complete; the phase 2 and 3 tabs explain that a full",
      "check is needed for clustering and keys."),
    full = paste(
      "Every row of every table is profiled, so distinct counts and uniqueness are exact and phases 2 and 3 are",
      "produced: the table clusters with a proposed canonical member for each group, the primary key candidates, and",
      "the foreign key candidates with their evidence and confidence. On a large SQL Server warehouse this is the",
      "slower run; on DuckDB and Parquet it is usually the quicker one.")
  )
  for (i in seq_len(nrow(runs))) {
    cat(sprintf("\n## %s report\n\n", tools::toTitleCase(runs$label[i])))
    cat(blurb[[runs$label[i]]], "\n\n")
    cat(sprintf('<p><a class="btn btn-primary" href="../%s" target="_blank" rel="noopener">Open the %s report</a> <span class="text-muted">(opens in a new tab, %.1f MB, rendered %s)</span></p>\n\n',
                runs$file[i], runs$label[i], runs$size_mb[i], runs$rendered_at[i]))
  }
}
```

To make one for your own database:

```r
library(DBinventory)
inventory_run("Driver={ODBC Driver 18 for SQL Server};Server=...;Database=...;Trusted_Connection=yes;",
              organisation = "Your NHS Trust", store = "dw_inventory.sqlite", report = "dw_inventory.html")
```
